html:
Tengizchevroil is the joint venture that runs the giant Tengiz oil field on the northeast shore of the Caspian Sea in Kazakhstan. It was formed in April 1993, the first big Western oil deal in the former Soviet Union.

Soviet geologists found Tengiz in 1979. Its oil lies deep and is full of poisonous hydrogen sulphide, which made it hard to develop with Soviet technology. After the Soviet Union broke up, President Nursultan Nazarbayev gave the American company Chevron a 40-year deal. Today Chevron holds half, ExxonMobil a quarter, the Kazakh state company KazMunayGas a fifth, and the Russian company Lukoil the rest.

Most of its oil leaves through the Caspian Pipeline Consortium line to the Russian Black Sea coast. Tengiz, with the later Kashagan field, made oil the heart of Kazakhstan's economy.
